docs.title: What Super Individuals CIC Is
docs.text:
Super Individuals CIC is a course and membership community focused on building real, owned AI agent systems. We bring together professionals, builders, and curious minds, teach them to build hands-on, then give them a long-term community in which to keep building.

We exist to help individuals become AI-native builders, not just consumers of AI — and to do it in the open, with public proof of work.

CPD status: Super Individuals CIC is a member of The CPD Certification Service (Membership No. 22924).

docs.title: Our Social Purpose
docs.text:
Super Individuals is a Community Interest Company (CIC) registered in England and Wales. A CIC is a company created specifically to serve a community rather than private shareholders.

Our purpose is public-interest: to widen access to practical, domain-specific AI capability so that individuals — not only large institutions — can build and deliver things that matter.

Asset lock for the mission

As a CIC, our assets and any surplus are subject to a statutory asset lock: they are dedicated to our social purpose and cannot be extracted as private profit. If the company is ever dissolved, remaining assets pass to another asset-locked, public-interest body.

Why this matters for partners

For organisations working with us on training or CSR-aligned programmes, the CIC structure means investment in our work stays committed to community benefit — and supports applications for grants and mission-aligned funding.

docs.title: 2. What the programme is
docs.text:
The programme is a live, online, cohort-based course delivered over two weeks, comprising two modules:

  • Module 1 — Intro Track: deploying and securing an AI agent on infrastructure you control, agent identity and behaviour design, and publishing a documentation portfolio.
  • Module 2 — Builder Track: node-based orchestration, connecting an autonomous agent runtime, and designing an MVP architecture for your own system.

Each day combines a scheduled session — an introductory meeting, an optional office-hours surgery, or a facilitated group call — with guided self-directed learning supported through our Discord community.

The programme comprises 30 hours of structured, directed learning. Live sessions are recorded and made available to participants during the programme.

Cohorts are capped at 15 participants and require a minimum of 12 to run. Section 8 explains what happens if we do not reach the minimum.

The cancellation period expires 14 days from the day after the contract is concluded (that is, the day after we send your booking confirmation).

docs.title: 6. Our additional guarantees
docs.text:
These guarantees are offered in addition to your legal rights. Where these guarantees and your legal rights would produce different outcomes, whichever is more favourable to you applies.

docs.text:

Minor changes. We may make minor changes to the curriculum, the tools used, or the facilitators delivering sessions — for example, where a third-party service changes or a facilitator is unavailable. We will not make changes that materially reduce what the programme delivers.

  • An autonomous agent runtime connected into your orchestration layer
  • MVP architecture for your own system, designed against a real use case

docs.text:
Q: Is the course CPD certified?

Super Individuals CIC is a member organisation of The CPD Certification Service (Membership No. 22924). This course's accreditation submission is currently under assessment. If accreditation is not in place for your cohort we will tell you before it begins, and you may cancel for a full refund if that materially affects your reason for booking.

Q: I'm not technical. Can I still do this?

Yes. No prior programming or server administration experience is required — you need basic computer literacy, a machine that can run a browser and a terminal, and a reliable connection. Module 1 is built for people meeting this material for the first time.

Q: What if I can't attend a session live?

Live sessions are recorded and made available to participants during the course. Occasionally a single session may need to be rescheduled; we give as much notice as we can and a recording is always made available.

A cohort runs only if it reaches 12 participants. We confirm whether your cohort is going ahead no later than 7 days before the scheduled start. If we do not reach the minimum, you choose between a place on the next cohort or a full refund, paid within 14 days.

Q: How much will the third-party services cost me?

Typically under US$30 in total across the course, and we configure hard spend caps on the first day. We credit back up to US$30 of documented costs when you complete. The n8n instance is on us.

Yes — where an organisation books and pays, the contract is with that organisation and is not a consumer contract, so the statutory cancellation right does not apply. The booking guarantees still apply as a matter of contract. We can provide an invoice and a one-page syllabus summary for internal approval on request. See section 15 of the Booking Terms.

You have a statutory right to cancel within 14 days of your booking confirmation, plus the guarantees above. Send a clear statement to register@sicic.org, or use the model cancellation form in the Booking Terms.

docs.text:
The live demo starts with a concrete problem: free-tier services give individuals enough infrastructure to build real products, but most people do not know which parts still exist, which ones still work, or how to combine them reliably.

Output

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Defining an AI agent's persona in a consistent, reusable way is hard.

Builders often write ad-hoc system prompts that are unstructured, hard to maintain, and difficult to port across different environments such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cowork, or custom runtimes.

That creates a practical gap: there is no repeatable method for capturing an agent's character, identity, user relationship, available tools, and routines as discrete artifacts that can be reviewed, versioned, reused, and improved.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
Johannes' project, agent-character-creator, is a skill that interviews the builder and generates a complete structured agent definition.

Instead of leaving the persona inside one long prompt, the skill splits the definition into five files:

  • SOUL.md captures character, values, and operating principles.
  • IDENTITY.md defines who the agent is.
  • USER.md defines who the agent serves and the relationship it should maintain.
  • TOOLS.md records the capabilities and tool context available to the agent.
  • ROUTINES.md defines recurring behaviours, patterns, and expected operating habits.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text:
Reusable agent design needs more than a good system prompt. It needs structure.

By turning persona design into separate files, agent-character-creator makes agent definitions easier to maintain, compare, audit, and install across different harnesses.

The same definition can be used for fictional, real-world, or neutral personas. Because it is platform-agnostic, the generated skill folder can be dropped into a Claude harness or custom runtime without rewriting the agent from scratch.

docs.title: Project Direction
docs.text:
This project points toward a more disciplined way of building agents:

  • interviews replace blank-page prompt writing
  • personas become version-controllable artifacts
  • agent identity is separated from tools and routines
  • builders can move definitions between platforms without losing structure

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
NewsAware is built for a problem that matters in journalism and public information: language models can produce unsupported claims, hallucinated facts, and exaggerated framing.

The live demo presents a workflow that evaluates text against three core questions:

  • what is the sentiment?
  • what is the central claim?
  • is there enough evidence to trust it?

docs.title: Core Workflow
docs.text:
The published project describes a clear agent path:

  • input
  • analyze
  • check evidence
  • refine

In practice, that means the system:

  • extracts the key claim from a piece of text
  • checks whether supporting evidence is actually present
  • lowers or raises credibility based on the reasoning it can justify

docs.title: Why Vivek Built This
docs.text:
NewsAware sits at an important intersection: AI systems, trust, and mental-health-adjacent information environments.

For a research scientist working across AI and mental health, credibility is not an abstract metric. It shapes how people interpret risk, uncertainty, and public claims. This project turns that concern into a concrete agent workflow.

docs.title: Example Use Case
docs.text:
The live demo shows the system handling claims that use vague sourcing, overstatement, or conspiracy framing.

Instead of simply classifying text, NewsAware explains why a claim is weak:

  • serious conclusions without verifiable sources
  • vague attribution such as "reports" or "studies show"
  • no cited data, institution, or study
  • framing that implies suppression without evidence

docs.title: Future Direction
docs.text:

  • knowledge graph integration
  • retrieval-based evidence checking
  • multi-step evaluation agents

These are good examples of Builder-track thinking: start with a simple working loop, then extend it toward stronger evidence systems and broader orchestration.

docs.text:
This is a strong founding cohort example because it turns a high-level concern about misinformation into a practical agent pattern. The project is narrow enough to be testable, but important enough to matter outside the demo itself.

It shows how SICIC projects can become applied research artifacts, not just technical exercises.

Marketing science and data strategy depend on disciplined interpretation: understanding what the data can say, what it cannot say, and how decision-makers should act on the signal.

Nigel's lab turns that advisory pattern into an agent system. The agents can support structured thinking, strategy development, and practical interpretation of business and customer signals.

docs.title: Genie
docs.text: Genie represents the advisory side of the lab: a guide for turning a prompt, question, or unclear strategic situation into a more structured path forward.

docs.title: Bin Vader
docs.text: Bin Vader adds a sharper operational role to the showcase. Its inclusion makes the project less generic and shows that useful agent systems can have distinct voices and jobs rather than one flat assistant persona.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text:
This is a useful founding cohort example because it shows the move from one-agent experimentation into a portfolio of agents.

For marketing science and data strategy work, that matters: different business questions often need different reasoning modes, levels of skepticism, and output styles.

Stack

Remotion + React 19 + AI

Strict TypeScript, AI-assisted research, MiniMax TTS, and code-driven rendering.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
HackStudio Pro treats video production as a software problem rather than a manual editing workflow.

The published demo shows a system designed to:

  • research across 17+ platforms
  • produce bilingual output in Chinese and English
  • work from a single codebase
  • reduce manual editing dependency
  • validate output before expensive renders

docs.title: Core Idea
docs.text:
The site frames the problem directly: making one high-quality documentary takes weeks, doing it in two languages doubles the work, and scaling by hand becomes unrealistic.

HackStudio Pro collapses that workflow by turning each stage of production into code.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
The live demo describes an end-to-end pipeline from raw sources to rendered .mp4, including:

  • concept
  • research
  • script
  • B-roll sourcing
  • editor pass
  • TTS generation
  • build
  • validation harness
  • render

docs.title: Architecture Highlights
docs.text:
According to the live site, some of the key architectural ideas are:

  • scripts are represented as TypeScript data
  • timing is computed from audio rather than manual timeline dragging
  • animations are React components
  • bilingual output is driven from one codebase
  • each narration line has a typed kind that selects the right renderer

docs.title: Auto-director for B-roll
docs.text: The demo includes a video-editor skill that reads the script, scores it against different documentary director profiles, and proposes B-roll choices that feel edited rather than merely assembled.

docs.title: Pre-render validation harness
docs.text:
Before rendering, the system runs five checks to catch avoidable mistakes:

  • counts consistency
  • TTS integrity
  • breathing time
  • B-roll overlap
  • text density

docs.title: Technology
docs.text:
The live demo lists a stack that includes:

  • Remotion 4.0
  • React 19
  • TailwindCSS v4
  • TypeScript
  • MiniMax TTS
  • OpenAI Whisper
  • OpenRouter Vision
  • Bun

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text: This is one of the strongest examples so far of a founding cohort member turning AI into owned production infrastructure. It is not just a prompt workflow or a single-purpose bot. It is a full publishing system with research, editorial logic, rendering, and validation built in.

docs.title: Closing Thought
docs.text: HackStudio Pro shows what it looks like when agentic systems are used not only to automate tasks, but to redesign an entire creative production pipeline around code, structure, and repeatability.

Berfu's project is an agent concept for organising work from natural instructions.

The agent takes the user's input, turns it into a full to-do list, proposes next steps, and helps the user decide what should happen first based on urgency.

docs.title: Why Berfu Built This
docs.text:
Senior customer experience, growth, FMCG, retail, and circular economy work can produce many competing priorities at once.

The value of this agent is not only task capture. It is the ability to turn unstructured instructions into an ordered, practical execution plan that keeps momentum visible.

docs.title: How It Helps
docs.text:
The agent is designed to support:

  • capturing instructions without losing detail
  • converting broad goals into concrete tasks
  • identifying urgent items
  • proposing immediate next steps
  • guiding follow-through instead of leaving the user with a static list

docs.title: Why It Matters

This is a useful founding cohort example because it focuses on a common executive problem: translating intent into action.

The agent creates a bridge between strategic direction and daily execution, especially when a user needs prioritisation rather than another generic note-taking tool.

docs.title: Why Jaidev Built This
docs.text:
The live site frames the project clearly: Jaidev wanted to build something he actually owns, not just use someone else's AI tool.

This lab documents both what he built and what went wrong along the way.

docs.title: Nova
docs.text:
Nova is Jaidev's Content Intelligence Officer, focused on YouTube discovery and summarisation.

According to the live demo, Nova:

  • searches YouTube through the Data API v3 via a custom MCP server
  • delivers the top 3 videos with 3-bullet summaries to Telegram
  • supports deeper analysis on request by replying with a number
  • manages topics through /topics commands

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
ZeroClaw acts as the manager. It receives commands through Telegram, delegates YouTube work to Nova, then renders thumbnails and presents the results.

Nova stays focused on content analysis.

The published pipeline is:

  • MCP server
  • Python fetcher
  • YouTube Data API v3

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text:
This is a strong founding cohort project because it turns a common AI use case, content discovery, into an owned operating workflow with clear delegation, controlled topics, and lightweight delivery through Telegram.

It is not just a chatbot. It is a managed content intelligence system with a defined role for the manager, a focused specialist agent, and a custom tool layer underneath.
